title: Model hard constraints separately from soft preferences (P1.9)
body:
## Role
A backend engineer separating what the household must have from what it would like.

## Goal
Model hard constraints separately from soft preferences (P1.9) so adapters can't silently weaken them.

## Context
Today dietary restrictions are a free-text preference and brand rules are avoid/prefer. An adapter needs typed constraints it can map, or refuse to map.

## Deliverables
Typed `HardConstraint` (allergen exclusion, dietary rule, do-not-substitute) and `SoftPreference` (brand, size, organic, generic) on the household and per item; a review requirement when no candidate can satisfy a hard constraint.

## Concrete examples
"No peanut products" is a hard allergen exclusion; "prefer Clover" is a soft brand preference.

## Constraints
Adapters receive only the constraints and preferences they need, never free-form household notes.

## Dependencies
#133.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Existing preferences migrate without loss.
- [ ] A plan line carries its applicable hard constraints.
- [ ] Tests prove a hard constraint can't be downgraded to a preference by any code path.

## Testing requirements
Migration tests on SQLite and Postgres; unit tests for constraint resolution.

## Out of scope
Instacart filter mapping (#147).

## Documentation requirements
README Data Model; preferences UI copy.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
